name: Gamma Communications plc
executive_summary: Gamma Communications is a UK-headquartered, pan-European provider of business cloud communications, voice enablement and connectivity, sold primarily through channel partners to SMEs and directly to enterprise and public-sector clients. The quantitative screen flags the name as a buy on cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk metrics (P/E 14.1, P/B 2.3, ROE 17.2%, debt/equity 13%), but an earnings-basis overlay already downgrades the raw signal to Hold where statutory and adjusted EPS diverge. Filings show a durable 89% recurring-revenue model and strong adjusted cash generation, with FY2025 revenue of £645.8m (+11%) and adjusted EBITDA of £141.7m (+13%), though statutory PBT fell to £87.7m on £10.6m of exceptional items and UK SME gross profit declined. The central debate is whether German M&A (Starface, Placetel) and cloud migration can offset UK macro/PSTN-transition headwinds, and whether a possible Epiris/Providence takeover crystallises value before integration risk materialises.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Gamma offers a rare combination of recurring SaaS-like revenue, self-funded growth and shareholder returns at a mid-teens multiple. The screen passes Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple and Earnings Quality — five factor families in total — on full data quality (20/20 metrics). That profile fits a capital-light, high-ROCE compounder: FY2025 ROCE was 27.8% (2024 pro forma: 27.4%), adjusted cash conversion 93%, and the business has compounded revenue from £191.8m to £645.8m over ten years (13% CAGR) per the FY2025 annual report.

The value case is not purely statistical. Network ownership, a 1,500+ partner channel and leading UK cloud seat scale create switching costs; Germany offers a structural growth runway with lower cloud penetration. Capital returns are explicit: £45.1m buyback in H1 2025, a further programme announced for FY2026–27, and a board intention to fix the dividend at FY2025 levels for two years (aggregate return of up to c.£125m). At ~14x earnings and ~2.3x book, the market appears to discount UK softness and integration execution rather than franchise quality — which is where the screen finds opportunity, albeit with the screen's own Hold overlay on adjusted vs statutory earnings.
financial_review:
**Source coverage:** Five consolidated annual Companies House accounts are available (FY2021–FY2025 bodies present). **No interim, half-year or trading-update RNS filings are indexed** — H1 2026 trends cannot be verified from primary regulatory sources in this pack.

**Revenue and profitability (annual filings, primary source)**

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Revenue | £484.6m | £521.7m | £579.4m | £645.8m |
| Gross profit | £247.7m | £267.2m | £300.3m | £348.2m |
| Statutory PBT | £64.9m | £71.5m | £95.6m | £87.7m |
| Adjusted EBITDA | £105.1m | £114.3m | £125.5m | £141.7m |
| Adjusted PBT | — | — | £111.9m | £119.4m |
| Adjusted EPS (diluted) | 71.8p | 75.1p | 85.1p | 94.5p |
| Statutory EPS (diluted) | 50.6p | — | 72.0p | 69.3p |
| Recurring revenue | — | — | 89% | 89% |

*(FY2022–FY2023 from Companies House annual bodies; FY2024–FY2025 highlights from FY2025 annual body; FY2024 adjusted EPS/dividend detail from FY2024 annual body.)*

Trend: Top-line growth has been consistent (+11% in both FY2024 and FY2025), with gross profit growing faster (+16% in FY2025) as Germany scales. On an **adjusted** basis, earnings momentum remains positive (+11% adjusted EPS in FY2025). **Statutory** PBT fell 8% to £87.7m in FY2025, reflecting £10.6m of exceptional items including £3.3m UK restructuring costs (expected to save £7m p.a. from FY2026). The screen's earnings-basis overlay — statutory EPS down 4% to 69.3p while adjusted EPS rose — is supported by filing data and warrants caution on headline P/E.

**Cash, balance sheet and capital allocation**

- FY2025 adjusted cash from operations: **£131.8m** (+9%; conversion 93%).
- FY2024 cash from operations: **£116.8m** (−5% vs £123.5m in FY2023, reflecting one-off working-capital benefits in the prior year).
- FY2025 net debt: **£9.3m** vs net cash **£153.7m** at FY2024 year-end, after Starface acquisition (£152.2m), buyback (£45.1m) and dividends (£18.9m).
- First use of debt: **£130m multicurrency revolving credit facility** drawn partially for Starface (FY2025 annual report).
- FY2024 year-end net cash **£153.7m** (FY2024 annual report); FY2022 net cash **£92.5m**.

**Yahoo fallback (balance-sheet detail not in filing highlights):** Goodwill rose to **£214m** at FY2025 (from £115.2m in FY2024 per Yahoo), consistent with Starface/Placetel consolidation; tangible book turned **negative** at −£12.1m. Cash fell to **£23.7m** (Yahoo). Free cash flow **£64.1m** in FY2025 (Yahoo; filing cites adjusted cash metrics only).

**Segment/geographic colour (FY2025 annual report):** German gross profit grew nearly 200% post-Starface/Placetel, offsetting a **decline in UK SME gross profit** despite higher cloud volumes. PSTN switch-off (January 2027) is driving fibre migration but compresses margins as legacy higher-margin products roll off. Group gross margin increased to **54%**.

**Gaps:** No indexed interim results for H1 2026. Detailed going-concern and principal-risk narrative pages (referenced at pp. 36–43 of FY2025 report) are **not present in the extracted filing bodies** — risk assessment relies on strategic-report language and news.
risks_and_flags:
**UK cyclical/migration risk:** Management explicitly cites a challenging UK macro backdrop, subdued SME spending, and PSTN-to-fibre transition pressure on connectivity pricing and margins. Cloud seat volumes rose but UK SME gross profit fell — a mix issue screens do not capture.

**Competitive pressure:** Enterprise pricing remains competitive; hyperscale/cloud vendors (Microsoft Teams, Cisco) are both partners and competitors. Gamma's moat depends on channel relationships and network ownership, but margin defence in connectivity is uncertain.

**M&A and leverage:** Starface (£152.2m) materially increased goodwill and moved the balance sheet from net cash to net debt. Integration execution across Germany/Placetel/Starface platforms is early-stage ("progressing well" per FY2025 report). Yahoo shows goodwill at 56% of total assets — acquisition impairment risk if UK growth stalls.

**Regulatory:** Operates in regulated telecoms markets (Ofcom PSTN switch-off cited). Network compliance and numbering obligations are ongoing; no specific enforcement actions in sources.

**Governance/management:** CFO Bill Castell departs 31 March 2026; Damien Maltarp appointed (joins later 2026). Chair acknowledged **disappointing share price performance**. Board gender/ethnicity targets not met (75% male, no ethnically diverse directors post-AGM).

**Takeover uncertainty:** Epiris LLP and Providence Equity Partners L.L.C. linked to possible offers (Rule 2.4/2.8). PUSU deadline extended to **2 September 2026**; discussions with "other potential offerors" ongoing. No firm offer — binary outcome risk for standalone holders. Buybacks continue during the offer period (~980p average), which supports per-share value but reduces free float.

**Accounting/earnings quality:** Divergence between adjusted EPS (+11% to 94.5p) and statutory EPS (−4% to 69.3p) is material; screen overlay already flags this. FY2023 included £16m goodwill impairment (Spanish CGU, FY2022 body).

**Filing gaps:** Going-concern assessment, covenant terms on the £130m RCF, and pension disclosures are **not available** in extracted bodies — cannot verify from this pack.

news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is **skewed toward takeover speculation and buyback mechanics**; limited sell-side or trade-press fundamental depth.

**M&A / takeover (material):**
- *Gamma Confirms Takeover Talks As Shares Jump 14.7%* (Yahoo Finance, 8 April 2026) — early-stage discussions, Barclays advising.
- *Gamma Communications shares surge 13% after confirming takeover talks* (Investing.com UK, 8 April 2026).
- *Gamma Communications Soon To Be Acquired? If So, What's A Fair Price?* (Seeking Alpha, 21 April 2026).
- *Possible offer for Gamma Communications Plc* (Epiris RNS/Investegate, 24 June 2026) — Epiris considering offer; follows Providence Rule 2.8.
- *Further extension of PUSU Deadline* (Gamma RNS, 5 August 2026) — Epiris deadline to 2 September 2026; other offerors in discussion.

**Results / strategy:**
- *Gamma boosted by M&A but domestic sales weigh on shares* (Investors' Chronicle, 24 March 2026).
- *GAMA: Strong German growth drove 11% revenue and 16% gross profit gains* (TradingView, 24 March 2026).
- *How The Gamma Communications (LSE:GAMA) Narrative Is Shifting With Recut Targets And New CFO* (Yahoo Finance, 8 April 2026) — analyst fair-value cuts alongside takeover news.

**Capital returns:**
- Sustained buyback activity through August 2026 at ~965–990p (multiple Kalkine Media articles, 6–11 August 2026; RNS *Transaction in Own Shares*, 5–13 August 2026).
- *Gamma Communications Advances Share Buyback, Reducing Outstanding Shares to 91 Million* (Kalkine Media, 21 July 2026).

**Governance:**
- CFO transition and Main Market/FTSE 250 inclusion referenced in FY2025 annual report (May–June 2025).

News is **not thin on event-driven items** but **thin on independent operational analysis** post-FY2025 results — most Google hits are syndicated Kalkine content or takeover-related.
research_rationale: Filings confirm the screen's quality-and-cash compounder thesis, but UK SME weakness, post-acquisition leverage, statutory/adjusted earnings divergence and unresolved takeover process limit full confirmation of the raw Buy signal.
